findings.premise: The new module covers the ISSUE's whole fix intent: it owns the lease, the generation/supersede rules and the running process; it lets the panel start, report, stop and ask whether a turn is running; and it gets its own unit tests.
findings.evidence: The ISSUE's fix intent (ISSUE.md:15) asks for: start a turn and wait for its lease, report events, stop, 'say whether one is running', own the lease, generation and supersede rules and the process, and unit tests. The LLD covers each one: start/stop/detach/invalidate, `live` (whether a turn is running), the state moved from chat-panel.ts:142-177, acquireSessionLease/runLeased/followLiveTurn/stopLive/stopActive/detachActive, and turn-lifecycle.test.ts. The panel keeps webview wiring, titles and permission/selection handling, as the ISSUE says it should. [files: docs/standalone/defect-vscode-plugin-src-chat-chat-E202610108ca7382b/ISSUE.md, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: Today, a superseded or disposed turn keeps reading but posts nothing. At its terminal event it clears its cursor and returns the iterator. Only the current generation posts the waiting status and the lock error.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:900-906: `if (disposed || myGen !== generation) { if (next.value.kind === 'done' || ... 'error') { clearCursor(...); void iterator.return?.(undefined); break; } continue; }`. Lines 757 and 765 gate the waiting post and the 'could not lock chat session' post on `!disposed && myGen === generation`. Line 762 returns silently on LockWaitAborted/LockWaitSuperseded, and lines 770-773 release the lease when the turn is no longer current after the grant. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: Today, a done/error event clears the cursor before the session is saved. Saving at a done uses the throwing deps.store.save, not trySave. A throw in the run posts an error with activeTurnId ?? 'none' and saves the session.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:931 runs `clearCursor(ev.turnId)` before the `deps.store.save(s)` calls at 934 and 941. Line 933 sets nativeSessionId on a done. The catch at 948-952 posts `{kind:'error', turnId: activeTurnId ?? 'none', ...}` and then calls trySave(s), only when current. This matches LLD §2.2 and the onTerminal note 'store.save, which may throw'. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: The panel's call sites that the lifecycle must take over are complete: runTurn, followLiveTurn (postInitialState and open-chat), cancel-turn, new-chat/open-chat with their ++generation, the permission-decision relay, dispose, adopt, and channel onDidDispose.
findings.evidence: A grep of chat-panel.ts finds every use: stopActive at 1014 (cancel-turn); detachActive at 1026/1046 (each followed by ++generation at 1027/1047), 1181 (onDidDispose), 1203 (adopt) and 1214 (dispose); followLiveTurn at 339 (postInitialState) and 1052; activeProvider/activeTurnId at 1120-1122 (permission-decision, which the LLD maps to `live`). No other code outside the turn machinery reads generation, waitCtl, liveProc or runningTurns. extension.ts:52/588 imports DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, and the LLD keeps that import working through a re-export. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts]

findings.premise: TurnLifecycleDeps.processStartTime has the type (pid: number) => number | null and takes what the panel resolves today.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:98 declares `readonly processStartTime?: ((pid: number) => number | undefined) | undefined;`. session-lock.ts:322 declares `export function defaultProcessStartTime(pid: number): number | undefined`. Line 851 turns undefined into null itself (`startTime(proc.pid) ?? null`). Under strict TS, passing the panel's resolved `startTime` into a dep typed `number | null` fails tsc. That breaks the LLD's own 'plugin tsc --noEmit clean' acceptance check. Type the dep as `number | undefined` and keep the `?? null` inside the module. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/session-lock.ts]
findings.action: Change TurnLifecycleDeps.processStartTime to `(pid: number) => number | undefined` (matching ChatPanelHostDeps and defaultProcessStartTime), and keep the `?? null` coercion when writing liveTurn.startedAt.

findings.premise: Invariant: Stop ends both the live turn and the followed turn. A chat switch, close or adopt only detaches a session-file turn and stops a pipe turn. The LLD's stop()/detach() reproduce stopActive/detachActive, and invalidate() reproduces the separate ++generation.
findings.evidence: stopActive (712-718) aborts following, stops resumedProc and calls stopLive. stopLive (678-709) aborts waitCtl, returns the iterator, calls providers.get(prov).cancel(tid) and stops liveProc, swallowing each failure. detachActive (725-739) detaches only when `detachLive !== undefined && liveProc?.cursor !== undefined` and otherwise calls stopLive. detachThis (888-893) removes the turn id from runningTurns and saves. The generation bump after detachActive is a separate statement (1027/1047), which matches the separate invalidate(). The LLD's stop, detach and invalidate contracts and its edge-case table match all of this. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]

findings.premise: Invariant: one CLI process per session. The lease is released when the process exits, not when its answer ends, through runLeased's attach in onSpawn. An adapter without onSpawn releases on return.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:829-834: `await runLeased(lease, async (attachLease) => { const onSpawn = (proc) => { attachLease(proc); ...`. session-lock.ts:142 exports `runLeased<T>(lease, body: (attach) => Promise<T>)`. The comment at 827-828 says it 'releases the lease on every path unless a process was attached'. The LLD moves this block unchanged into start() (§2.2 postconditions and the edge-case table). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/session-lock.ts]

findings.premise: Each acceptance criterion has a test that fails without the fix. ac1 is proved by new turn-lifecycle.test.ts unit cases, one per lifecycle rule, using the existing fixtures (fakeLiveProc, waitFor, tick) and createMemorySessionLocks. ac2 is proved by the unchanged chat-panel and extension-wiring suites plus a clean tsc.
findings.evidence: turn-lifecycle.ts does not exist yet, so every ac1 unit case fails to import without the fix. The fixtures exist: __tests__/fixtures.ts:54 `export const tick`, :57 `export async function waitFor`, :82 `export function fakeLiveProc`. session-lock.ts:164 exports createMemorySessionLocks. The listed subjects cover every error path and edge case in §4 (supersede while waiting/reading, grant after stale, lock failure, throw in the run, cursor throttle and clear, stop idempotent, detach for session-file vs pipe, follow skip/takeover, invalidate, live). ac2 is a regression guard, and the extracted code must be in place for it to pass. One note: chat-panel.test.ts has 104 `test(`/`it(` lines, not the '111 cases' the LLD states. This does not affect the tests themselves. summary.prose: The chat panel's turn machinery moves out of createChatPanelHost into a new vscode-free module, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts. The module runs a turn for a session: it waits for the session's lease, applies the newest-message-wins rule, keeps the running CLI process, records where the turn's output is in the session file, follows a saved turn after a reload, and stops or detaches on request. The panel keeps the webview, the transcript rows, titles, and permission and selection handling, and hands the module a set of callbacks. Behaviour does not change, and the module gets its own tests.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Move the chat turn and lease lifecycle out of createChatPanelHost into its own module

api.name: createTurnLifecycle
api.signature: export function createTurnLifecycle(deps: TurnLifecycleDeps): TurnLifecycle; interface TurnLifecycleDeps { readonly providers: ProviderRegistry; readonly store: Pick<ChatSessionStore, 'save'>; readonly locks: SessionLocks; readonly lockTimeoutMs: () => number; readonly hostPid: number; readonly processStartTime: (pid: number) => number | undefined; readonly isAlive: (pid: number) => boolean; readonly isOpen: () => boolean; readonly logger: ChatPanelLogger }

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: What the panel resolves today at chat-panel.ts:146-149 and 171 (locks default createMemorySessionLocks, hostPid default process.pid, processStartTime/isAlive defaults from session-lock.ts, lockTimeoutMs default DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS), plus isOpen = the panel's !disposed, and store.save for trySave. processStartTime keeps the panel's type (pid) => number | undefined (chat-panel.ts:98, session-lock.ts:322); the module turns undefined into null when it writes liveTurn.startedAt, as chat-panel.ts:851 does.

returns.meaning: One per panel host; holds the state now at chat-panel.ts:142-177 that concerns turns: activeTurnId, activeProvider, activeIterator, generation, runningTurns, following, resumedProc, detachLive, waitCtl, liveProc.

preconditions: Called once from createChatPanelHost, after the panel resolves its defaults.
postconditions: No turn is running and live is undefined.

api.name: TurnLifecycle.start
api.signature: start(session: ChatSession, req: TurnRequest, sink: TurnSink): Promise<void>; interface TurnSink { onWaiting(): void; beforeRun(): Promise<void>; onEvent(ev: TurnEvent): void; onTerminal(ev: TurnEvent & { kind: 'done' | 'error' }): void; onError(message: string, turnId: string): void }

parameters.name: session
parameters.purpose: The session the turn runs for; the module sets its liveTurn and nativeSessionId and saves it.

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: Built by the panel exactly as at chat-panel.ts:820-823 (prompt, cwd, permissionMode, allowedTools, resume).

parameters.name: sink
parameters.purpose: Panel callbacks: onWaiting posts the waiting status; beforeRun is governor.beginTurn; onEvent posts, appends and records pending permissions/selections and governor.observe; onTerminal saves (store.save, which may throw), governor.resolveTurn, postHistory; onError posts an error turn-event.

returns.meaning: Settles when the panel stops reading the turn (terminal event, supersede, detach, stop, or a drop while waiting). The process may keep running; the lease is released when it exits.

errors.condition: Every failure is reported through sink.onError (when current) and logged; start never rejects, so the panel's fire-and-forget call stays safe.

preconditions: Synchronously at the call: the pending lease wait is aborted and generation is bumped, as at chat-panel.ts:785-787 (moved after the echo, with no await between, so nothing observable changes).

No adapter for session.provider: sink.onError('no adapter for provider

', 'none') and return, as at 812-818.
postconditions: The lease is acquired through locks.acquire with timeoutMs = lockTimeoutMs() and released through runLeased: by the attached process's exit, otherwise on return.

Only while current (isOpen() and the generation unchanged) are onWaiting, onEvent, onTerminal and onError called. A superseded turn keeps reading but reports nothing; at its terminal event it clears its cursor and returns the iterator (900-906).

On spawn, if the process writes to the session file, session.liveTurn = {cursor, ownerHostPid: hostPid, pid, startedAt} is saved at once; progress updates the cursor and saves at most every CURSOR_SAVE_MS (500 ms); at the terminal event the cursor is cleared before onTerminal; a done event's sessionId is set as session.nativeSessionId before onTerminal.
A throw inside the run (beforeRun, adapter start, onTerminal's save) calls onError(message, activeTurnId ?? 'none') and then saves the session, when current.

api.name: TurnLifecycle.follow
api.signature: follow(session: ChatSession, sink: FollowSink): void; interface FollowSink { onEvent(ev: TurnEvent): void; onEnd(): void }

parameters.name: session
parameters.purpose: The session to resume; nothing happens unless it has a liveTurn this host may follow.

parameters.name: sink
parameters.purpose: onEvent gets every event (the panel appends it, and posts it only while the panel is open and this session is shown); onEnd runs after the cursor has been cleared and saved (the panel posts the history when the session is shown).

returns.meaning: Starts the resume in the background, as followLiveTurn does today (269-324).

errors.condition: adapter.resume throws: logged as a warning, the cursor stays saved.

preconditions: Skipped when: no liveTurn; this session is already being followed; the turn is running in this host (runningTurns); the owner host pid is not this host and is alive; there is no adapter or it has no resume.
postconditions: Takes ownership (ownerHostPid = hostPid, saved) before reading.
Cursor progress saved at most every CURSOR_SAVE_MS; a done event's sessionId becomes nativeSessionId; at the end (not aborted) the cursor is cleared if unchanged and the session saved.

returns.meaning: The Stop control (stopActive today, 712-718): aborts the lease wait and the follow, returns the iterator, cancels the provider turn, stops the live process and the resumed process. Resolves once they have exited.

errors.condition: Each step swallows its own failure, as stopLive does (678-709).

api.name: TurnLifecycle.detach

returns.meaning: A chat switch, panel close or adopt (detachActive today, 725-739): stops following; a turn writing to the session file keeps running with its lease and saved cursor; a pipe turn is stopped as by stop().

postconditions: live is undefined; the detached turn's id leaves runningTurns so a later follow can resume it.

api.name: TurnLifecycle.invalidate

returns.meaning: Bumps the generation so a running turn stops reporting (the ++generation after detachActive in new-chat and open-chat).

postconditions: The turn that was current is no longer current.

api.name: TurnLifecycle.live
api.signature: readonly live: { readonly provider: ProviderId; readonly turnId: string } | undefined

returns.meaning: The turn the panel is reading live, defined once its first event arrived; the panel's decision message uses it in place of activeProvider/activeTurnId.

errorCases.scenario: The lease cannot be acquired for a reason other than being dropped (lock dir unwritable, corrupt lock).
errorCases.detection: locks.acquire rejects with an error that is not LockWaitAborted or LockWaitSuperseded.
errorCases.response: Log an error and, when current, sink.onError('could not lock chat session: <msg>', 'none'); start returns without running.
errorCases.userImpact: An error line in the chat; the user can resend.

errorCases.scenario: The turn is dropped while waiting (a newer submit, Stop, chat switch, panel close).
errorCases.detection: locks.acquire rejects with LockWaitAborted or LockWaitSuperseded (the wait's AbortController was aborted).
errorCases.userImpact: None: the newer action takes over.

errorCases.scenario: The lease is granted after the turn stopped being current.
errorCases.detection: After acquire resolves, isOpen() is false or generation differs from the turn's.
errorCases.response: Release the lease and return without running.

errorCases.scenario: beforeRun (governor.beginTurn), adapter.run or onTerminal's store.save throws.
errorCases.detection: The try around the read loop inside runLeased catches it.
errorCases.response: When current, sink.onError(message, activeTurnId ?? 'none') and save the session; runLeased releases the lease unless a process was attached (then its exit releases it).
errorCases.userImpact: An error line; the transcript so far is kept.

errorCases.scenario: A save fails during cursor recording.
errorCases.response: Logged as a warning; the turn continues.
errorCases.userImpact: A reload may resume from an older cursor.

errorCases.detection: adapter.resume or its iteration throws inside follow's background task.
errorCases.response: Log a warning; following is cleared and resumedProc forgotten; the cursor stays saved.
errorCases.userImpact: The turn's remaining output is not shown until a later reopen succeeds.

errorCases.scenario: Stopping a process or cancelling a provider turn fails.
errorCases.detection: proc.stop() or providers.get(p).cancel(id) rejects or throws.
errorCases.response: Swallowed per step, as stopLive does; the remaining steps still run.

edgeCases.input: A second start() while the first turn is still waiting for its lease.
edgeCases.expected: The first wait is aborted and that turn is dropped; the second waits.

edgeCases.input: A second start() while the first turn is reading.
edgeCases.expected: The first turn stops reporting but keeps reading to its end (its CLI never stalls); the second waits for the first process to exit, then runs.

edgeCases.input: detach() while a session-file turn is running.
edgeCases.expected: The iterator is returned, the cursor is saved, the turn id leaves runningTurns, the process and lease stay; follow() on the session then resumes it.

edgeCases.input: detach() while a pipe turn (no cursor) is running.
edgeCases.expected: Same as stop(): the process is stopped.

edgeCases.input: follow() on a session whose turn is running in this host.
follow() when the cursor's owner is another live host.
edgeCases.expected: No-op; when that host is gone, this host takes ownership and follows.

edgeCases.input: invalidate() then the old turn's terminal event.
edgeCases.expected: No sink call; its cursor is cleared.

edgeCases.input: An adapter without onSpawn support (no process attached).
edgeCases.expected: runLeased releases the lease when start's body returns.

invariantsToPreserve.text: One CLI process per session: a turn waits for the session lease, stopping the previous process only after lockTimeoutMs; the lease is released when the process exits, not when its answer ends (acquireSessionLease and runLeased at chat-panel.ts:747-829).
Newest message wins: only the current generation posts; a superseded turn keeps reading to its terminal event (chat-panel.ts:900-906).
Stop ends the live and the followed turn; a chat switch, close or adopt only detaches a session-file turn (stopActive/detachActive called from cancel-turn vs new-chat/open-chat/dispose/adopt).
liveTurn is owned by one host; another host follows only once the owner pid is dead; the cursor is cleared at the terminal event (ChatSession.liveTurn).
ChatPanelHostDeps and chat-panel.ts exports, including DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS used by extension.ts:52, are unchanged.

testLevels.purpose: The lifecycle rules in isolation, with memory session locks, a fake ProviderRegistry whose adapter yields scripted TurnEvents and reports a fake TurnProcess through onSpawn, an in-memory store and a recording sink.
subjects: createTurnLifecycle start: waits for the lease, reports waiting, runs, lease released on process exit not at done
start supersede: a second start drops a waiting turn; a reading turn stops reporting but reads to its end
start not current after grant: lease released, nothing runs
start lock failure: onError('could not lock chat session: ...')
start throw inside the run (beforeRun rejects): onError with 'none' and the session saved; lease released
cursor: liveTurn set and saved on spawn, throttled progress saves, cleared at the terminal event before onTerminal; nativeSessionId set on done
stop: cancels the provider turn and stops the live and resumed processes; idempotent with nothing running
detach: a session-file turn keeps running, cursor saved, follow then resumes it; a pipe turn is stopped
follow: skipped for a running turn and for a live other owner; takes ownership from a dead owner; onEnd after the cursor is cleared
invalidate and isOpen=false: no sink calls
live: defined after the first event, undefined after stop/detach

alternativesConsidered.name: Turn lifecycle factory with a sink
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: createTurnLifecycle(deps) in a new chat/turn-lifecycle.ts owns lease, generation, process, cursor and follow; the panel passes a TurnSink of callbacks per turn.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New vscode-free module turn-lifecycle.ts exporting createTurnLifecycle(deps: {providers, store, locks, lockTimeoutMs, hostPid, processStartTime, isAlive, logger}) returning TurnLifecycle {start(session, req, sink), follow(session, sink), stop(), detach(), invalidate(), live}. It holds all of the state currently at chat-panel.ts:142-177 that concerns turns (activeTurnId, activeProvider, activeIterator, generation, runningTurns, following, resumedProc, detachLive, waitCtl, liveProc) and the bodies of acquireSessionLease, the runLeased block of runTurn, followLiveTurn, stopLive, stopActive and detachActive. A TurnSink carries the panel callbacks: isCurrent-aware onWaiting, onEvent(ev) (panel posts, appends, records pending perms/selections, governor.observe), onTerminal(ev) (save, governor.resolveTurn, postHistory), beforeRun (governor.beginTurn), onError(message). The panel keeps echo, title, request building, appendEvent and the message switch. CURSOR_SAVE_MS and DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS move to the module; chat-panel re-exports DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS so extension.ts is unchanged.
pros: Every lifecycle rule (supersede, wait-drop, lease follows process, detach vs stop, follow ownership) lives in one file testable with fake adapters and memory locks, no webview.
Panel's runTurn shrinks to prompt bookkeeping plus one start() call; the closure loses ~350 lines.
Public surface of chat-panel.ts and ChatPanelHostDeps is unchanged, so extension.ts and the 111 panel tests need no edits.
cons: The sink is a callback interface the panel must implement carefully to keep the 'post only while current' rule; the module must call it only for the current generation.
Two places now refer to the session object (panel's active session and the module's per-turn session) — must stay the same object.

alternativesConsidered.name: Event-emitter lifecycle object
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A TurnLifecycle class that emits typed events (waiting/event/terminal/error) the panel subscribes to once.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same state and rules as a1 but exposed as a class with on('event'|'terminal'|'waiting'|'error') subscriptions registered once at host creation; start(session, req) returns a promise. The panel subscribes in createChatPanelHost and routes events to post/appendEvent based on the session carried in each event.
pros: Panel wiring is set up once rather than per turn.
cons: The chat module uses factory functions returning plain objects (createSessionOutput, createFileSessionLocks), not classes with emitters; this would be a new idiom.
Events must carry the session to keep follow-vs-live routing right, adding a field the sink form gets for free.
Async listener errors are harder to contain than direct awaited callbacks (beforeRun must be awaited before spawn).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same ownership as a1 but a new idiom and weaker ordering guarantees for the awaited pre-spawn hook (partial on keeping behaviour).

alternativesConsidered.name: Split into two modules: lease runner and follower
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: turn-runner.ts for live turns (lease, generation, process) and turn-follower.ts for resuming saved turns, coordinated by the panel.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extract runTurn's lease and loop into createTurnRunner and followLiveTurn into createTurnFollower; the panel composes them and implements stopActive/detachActive by calling both.
cons: runningTurns is shared between the runner (adds on spawn) and the follower (skips running turns); Stop and detach must coordinate both, so the coupling stays in the panel — the opposite of the goal.
Stop/detach rules end up split across three places.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaves the coupling in the panel: partial on ownership and testability because Stop/detach and runningTurns stay coordinated by the panel.

citations.quotedText: import { createChatPanelHost, CHAT_VIEW_TYPE, DEFAULT_TURN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, type ChatPanelChannel } from './chat/chat-panel.js';
export async function runLeased<T>(lease: SessionLease, body: (attach: (proc: LeaseProcess) => void) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
